privacy.title: Privacy information
privacy.reviewNotice: Controller-approved privacy information, last updated 2026-07-23. Provider contracts and international-transfer safeguards are maintained separately in the processor register.
privacy.processingText: EngCRM is an internal B2B CRM for research, contact management and human-approved outreach.
privacy.leadProcessing: Lead management: business/contact details, research notes, interaction history and AI fit scores.
privacy.outreachProcessing: Outreach and inbox: recipient details, draft and sent messages, replies and opt-out records.
privacy.accountProcessing: Staff accounts: name, email, password hash, role, authentication and audit data.
privacy.cardProcessing: Business-card capture: card images, extracted contact details and optional capture location.
privacy.sourcesText: Business and contact data can be collected from public company websites, directories, business cards and public venue listings. We record the source where technically available.
privacy.recipientsText: The following processors may receive data when their feature is enabled. Applicable agreements and transfer safeguards are maintained in the controller's processor register.
privacy.retentionText: The application enforces configured deletion periods for leads, inbox messages, AI data, interaction records, audit records and stale push tokens. A deletion or erasure request removes directly linked CRM data; backups expire under the separately documented backup schedule.
privacy.rightsText: You may request access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection to processing, and data portability, and may lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority. To exercise a right or object to outreach, contact
privacy.noTrackingText: The web application uses only the session cookie required for authenticated operation. It does not use analytics, advertising or tracking cookies.

linkedin.import.title: Import LinkedIn connections
linkedin.import.step1: On LinkedIn open Settings → Data privacy → Get a copy of your data.
linkedin.import.step2: Choose "Connections" only and request the archive. LinkedIn emails a download link, usually within minutes.
linkedin.import.step3: Unzip it and upload Connections.csv below.
linkedin.import.emailNote: Most connections have no email address in the export: LinkedIn only includes emails that people chose to share. Name, company and position are always included.
linkedin.import.safeToRepeat: Safe to repeat: a newer export updates existing people and never overwrites what you typed.

linkedin.import.errorFailed: The import failed and nothing was saved. Try again; the server log has the details.
linkedin.matches.title: Match LinkedIn connections to organizations
linkedin.matches.intro: Each connection's company is compared with your organizations. Rows with an exact, unambiguous name match are pre-selected. Check them, change any that are wrong, then apply. "None of these" means the organization is not suggested for that person again.
linkedin.matches.empty: Nothing to match: every LinkedIn connection with a company is already linked or rejected.
linkedin.matches.loadFailed: Could not load the suggestions. Try again.
linkedin.cities.title: Cities for LinkedIn employers
linkedin.cities.intro: These organizations were created from your connections' employers. LinkedIn does not export a location, and the automatic lookup only accepts a city when exactly one place carries the company's name. Type a city (and a 2-letter country such as DE) or pick one the lookup offered; what you save here counts as entered by hand. Tick "stop asking" for entries that are not worth a city. Most connections first.

linkedin.jobChanges.title: Connections who may have changed jobs
linkedin.jobChanges.intro: A newer LinkedIn export shows these people at a different company than the one stored. Nothing was changed. "Moved" updates their company and position and unlinks them from the old organization — match or create the new one afterwards (Match to organizations, or the companies command). "Keep" means it is not a real move: the stored company stays and this change is not flagged again.

linkedin.companies.title: Create organizations from your connections' companies
linkedin.companies.intro: Each company your LinkedIn connections work at becomes an organization at stage Candidate, with its connections linked to it. The preview below writes nothing; it only counts what the button would do. A company that already exists with exactly the same name is reused, never duplicated, so this is safe to run again after every new import. LinkedIn exports no locations, so the new organizations have no city yet — that is the next step.

linkedin.lookup.title: Look up cities automatically
linkedin.lookup.intro: Each company name is sent to Google Places once (only the company name, never anything about the people) and the answer is remembered, so a company is never looked up or billed twice. A city is accepted only when exactly one place carries the company's name; anything unclear stays in the list below for you.

linkedin.lookup.nothing: Nothing to look up: every company has either been looked up already or has a city. ({{cached}} accepted cities are already applied.)
